extracted.intended_audience: Investigators preparing NIH R01 (PHS 398) applications and resubmissions
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and revising an NIH R01 application using the PHS 398 forms (including resubmission responses to prior reviews), ensuring required sections, biosketches, vertebrate/human subjects compliance, and reviewer-addressed revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Review Criterion: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project address an important problem? (Example criticism: 'Original proposal too broad in scope.' Response: sharpened the focus to be only about P. aeruginosa in chronic wounds.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate a clear, focused problem and translational relevance; if reviewers felt scope was too broad, narrow aims to a specific system/anatomical site and explicitly state how results will impact the field or lead toward treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Review Criterion: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the investigators well qualified? (Example criticism: 'PI Vernita Gordon is very junior and does not have enough related publications.' Response: list recent publications and collaborators adding deep expertise.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an explicit personal statement and biosketches showing relevant publications, leadership, and collaborators; address perceived gaps by documenting recent productivity and complementary expertise of collaborators.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Review Criterion: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project use novel concepts, approaches, or methods? (Example criticism: 'No explanation of how this study will lead to new targeted drug or treatment development.' Response: include Preliminary Studies indicating molecular mechanisms and how these point toward therapeutic strategies.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state novel aspects and mechanistic links to potential translational outcomes; include preliminary mechanistic data that support claims of innovation and future therapeutic directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Review Criterion: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the experimental design and methods well-reasoned and appropriate? (Criticisms noted: multiple mouse models/sites could introduce variability; lack of statistical treatment and quantifiable hypotheses; unclear experimental plans; insufficient preliminary data; uncertain microrheology feasibility; unnecessary methods such as PNA-FISH.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide rigorous, detailed experimental plans with clear statistical analyses, quantifiable hypotheses, contingencies if in vivo/in vitro disagree, justification for animal numbers, and method selection rationale (e.g., prioritize methods required for success; remove unnecessary assays). Consider reducing site/method multiplicity to limit confounders.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Review Criterion: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Will institutional setting and available resources contribute to success? (Criticisms included multiple performance sites and a foreign site making collaboration difficult.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document institutional support, specify performance sites and why they are appropriate, and minimize unnecessary multi-site complexity; ensure biosafety and animal facility certifications are described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission Response Expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: A resubmission must respond to prior Summary Statement criticisms with concrete changes and explanations (examples from the Summary Statement and applicant responses: sharpened focus, added measures of disease outcomes, sketched responses if in vivo/in vitro disagree, added in vivo validation Activity 3-3, published preliminary studies, clarified rheology plans, changed techniques like PNA-FISH to fluorescent bacteria, reduced to one mouse model/site, expanded statistical treatment, expanded Vertebrate Animals justification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When resubmitting, explicitly list each prior criticism and provide targeted modifications or rebuttals; add additional preliminary data or methodological details as needed; show how revisions directly address reviewer concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Research Plan: Required Sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Plan Section must include: Introduction (for resubmission/revision), Specific Aims, Research Strategy*, Progress Report Publication List, Protection of Human Subjects, Data Safety Monitoring Plan, Inclusion of Women and Minorities, Inclusion of Children, Vertebrate Animals, and Other Research Plan Sections (Select Agent Research; Multiple PD/PI Leadership Plan; Consortium/Contractual Arrangements; Letters of Support; Resource Sharing Plan(s); Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources; Appendix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the PHS 398 structure exactly; include each named subsection with appropriate detail and supporting documents (e.g., Vertebrate Animals, Human Subjects protections, resource sharing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects Section (Cover Page Supplement questions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify whether the proposed research is a Clinical Trial and whether it is an Agency-Defined Phase III Clinical Trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the appropriate boxes and provide requisite supporting documentation and protocols if human subjects or clinical trials are involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals Section (Cover Page Supplement and Research Plan)
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether vertebrate animals are euthanized. If 'Yes', indicate whether the method is consistent with American Veterinary Medical Association (AVMA) guidelines. If 'No' to AVMA guidelines, describe method and provide scientific justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document animal use clearly, justify numbers, provide AVMA-consistent euthanasia methods or scientifically justify deviations, and include expanded Vertebrate Animals detail when reviewers question animal numbers or care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Income Section (Cover Page Supplement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether program income is anticipated during the budget periods; if yes, provide format listing anticipated amounts and sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If program income is expected, list amounts, sources, and reflect them appropriately in the budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Embryonic Stem Cells Section
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether the project involves human embryonic stem cells. If Yes, list registration number(s) from the NIH registry or check that one from the registry will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide registry identifiers or confirm intent to use a registered cell line; if 'No', check the appropriate box.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventions and Patents Section (RENEWAL)
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether there are inventions and patents related to the project; if Yes, indicate whether they were previously reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose any inventions/patents and their reporting status per form instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of Investigator / Change of Institution Section
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide details when changing Project Director/Principal Investigator or grantee institution (names, former institution, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the change forms and supply required rationale/documentation if personnel or institutional changes occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosketch Content Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide Personal Statement, Education/Training, Positions and Honors, Contributions to Science, and complete list of Publications and Research Support for key personnel (formats exemplified by the biosketch pages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the PHS 398 biosketch format: emphasize relevance of experience to the project in Personal Statement, list relevant publications, and include current and pending support. Ensure contributions to science are concise and supported by references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget Justification Elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Justify costs such as tuition and fees, travel (to present data and for collaboration), supplies for culturing, publication costs, materials and supplies by year, and equipment maintenance (e.g., confocal microscope maintenance contract).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, line-itemed justifications tied to project activities; explain travel and training needs and include standard publication cost estimates when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosafety and Facility Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure animal work is done in a certified animal facility and in vitro work in appropriate BSL laboratories (example: P. aeruginosa is a BSL-2 organism; all in vitro work will be done in BSL-2 laboratories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State facility certifications, biosafety level of organism handling, and containment practices; reviewers expect appropriate biosafety planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical Analysis and Quantifiable Hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss statistical treatment, identification of potential relationships, and provide quantifiable hypotheses (criticism: lack of statistical treatment and quantifiable hypotheses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe statistical models, expected functional forms when supported by theory, sample size justification, and analysis plans; include details in Research Strategy and Vertebrate Animals sections as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary Data Requirement / Demonstration of Feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide adequate preliminary data to support feasibility (criticism: not enough preliminary data). Response: preliminary studies now published and referenced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include peer-reviewed preliminary studies where possible and reference them; explain how preliminary results support proposed aims and feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification for Animal Numbers and Experimental Design
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide justification for the requested number of animals (criticism: requested number of mice not well-supported; response: expanded Vertebrate Animals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include power calculations, expected effect sizes, and ethical justification; expand Vertebrate Animals section to address reviewer concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method Selection and Contingency Planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain rationale for chosen methods (e.g., microrheology vs AFM) and provide contingency plans if primary methods are not feasible or if in vivo and in vitro results differ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify which methods are essential versus auxiliary, provide fallback strategies, and describe validation experiments (e.g., in vivo validation of key in vitro findings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing and Authentication of Key Biological/Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Include Resource Sharing Plan(s) and Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State plans for data/material sharing and describe authentication procedures (e.g., cell line validation, reagent provenance) as required by the PHS 398 instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Support and Consortium/Contractual Arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide combined letters of commitment, letters of support from collaborators, and appropriate consortium or contractual documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include signed letters that document institutional commitments, collaborator roles, and any subcontracts; address prior reviewer concerns about foreign or multiple sites by amending letters accordingly.
